claims.finding: Braze affiliates filed eleven separate Form 144 sale notices across nine distinct dates in August 2026 (08/07, 08/10, 08/11, 08/13, 08/19 x2, 08/24 x2, 08/26, 08/27 x2) plus thirteen Form 4s on six dates (08/11, 08/12, 08/14, 08/19 x5, 08/21 x2, 08/26 x2, 08/28), against a 400-day baseline of one to four Form 144s per month arriving alongside a single-date vest batch of Form 4s (7 on 2026-02-02, 6 on 2026-02-20, 7 on 2026-03-20, 7 on 2026-05-19, 6 on 2025-11-20); four of the notices land on 08/24-08/27 as the stock printed its high close of $34.53.
claims.corpus_ref: filings.json, CIK 0001676238: Form 144 entries filing_date 2026-08-07 through 2026-08-27 and Form 4 entries 2026-08-11 through 2026-08-28, compared against the same file's 2025-09 to 2026-07 history
claims.why_not_priced: The news channel returned zero items for BRZE across all eleven sweeps and the only stored bodies are three StockTwits digests, none of which mentions insider selling; aggregators report individual Form 4 dollar amounts but not the month-over-month density of Form 144 notices, and a 144 is per-seller so eleven notices means many distinct sellers rather than one plan. If it were priced I would expect at least one captured item on it and I would not expect Barclays to be raising its target to $38 from $31 on 2026-09-03 into the same window.
claims.independence: Nothing else in this corpus points the same way, and one thing cuts against it: the stock had already surrendered the entire move, from $34.53 on 08/28 to $30.17 by the 09-08 midday mark (quote.json), which is consistent with the supply having been at least partly absorbed. Because Braze's fiscal Q2 ended 31 July and the release is 8 September, discretionary sales in late August would sit inside a normal blackout, so these are most likely pre-set 10b5-1 dispositions - which is why the number is small. none.
